accepts.because: redraw against a fresh picture of the colony NOW, rather than at the next tick; the hive ticks on its own, this is the extra one

the graph moved, so draw it again (GH #553). The app used to hold a `refresh` timer that asked `/colony/graph` every minute for a topology that only changes when somebody mutates it; the door below turns the receipt into this hive's own `in_refresh`, so the picture is exactly as fresh as the graph and costs nothing between two changes. The boot receipt is the first fill, which is what keeps a restarted screen from standing empty until the first mutation of the day

emits.because: one view towards a display; who that display is, is the wiring's question. The app says what the picture IS and says it whole; it does not know which surface will hold it, whether anybody is looking, or whether a second display holds the same view beside the first

description.purpose: An app: it draws the colony and hands the drawing to whoever is wired to hold it. A committed mutation takes a topology snapshot and a code cell turns it into one view -- a component tree plus the components it is written in. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS: params.ports is empty, so no edge reaches a cell in here; a caller names the hive and a lane on hop.route.
description.use_when: Somebody should see and rearrange what the colony knows, and a display is already there to show it. An app owns no channel and no port of its own, which is what lets the same drawing go to a display on a laptop, a display behind a proxy, or two displays at once, without this template knowing any of it.
description.not_in_scope: It draws nothing the topology snapshot does not hold, and it takes that snapshot on a mutation receipt through this hive's own lane to the colony's read-only graph endpoint (GH #163: that endpoint is one of the absolute endpoints a mutation may draw, because it is the sanctioned alternative to reading colony.db; the counts-never-content ledger endpoint joined it with GH #267). So the picture is as fresh as the graph itself. No port, no authentication, no TLS -- an app has no surface to protect, and whatever guards the display guards this too. No object vocabulary beyond cells, hives and edges. No stored camera: where a person is looking is theirs and stays in their browser.
description.contract_in: Two lanes, at the hive path. mutation_committed -- the mutation door's receipt (GH #553): the graph moved, so draw it again, and the BOOT receipt is what puts the first picture up. in_refresh -- take the topology snapshot now without changing anything, the operator gesture. The hive's own door turns the first into the second; which cell does the asking is this hive's business.
description.contract_out: One lane, out of the hive path. view -- the whole picture, ready to be laid on a surface. An edge from this hive to a display carries it and renames the lane to what the display accepts.
